title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 13: Augustine dissolves — election excites industry; despair is the impious' vice
pass_a_gloss: Solution. All these things are dissolved by Augustine in the places just cited; I answer nonetheless that the doctrine of election in all the pious excites and kindles the industry of living well. But if the impious and profane take thence occasion of torpor or despair, that happens by their vice and innate perversity, not by the doctrine itself.
pass_b_english: Sol. Augustine dissolves all this in the places just cited. Still I answer: the doctrine of election excites and kindles industry of living well in all the pious. If the impious and profane take from it occasion of torpor or despair, that is their vice and innate perversity — not the doctrine's.
source_text: Sol. Haec omnia dissolvuntur ab Augustino in locis modo citatis; Respondeo tamen, doctrinam electionis in piis omnibus excitare, et incendere industriam bene vivendi. Quod si impii et profani inde occasionem torporis aut desperationis accipiant, id fieri illorum vitio et innata perversitate, non ipsius doctrinae.
